primary_claim: Testing three SFT-based Blue Team approaches for eliciting true performance from an untrusted model prompted to sandbag on Olympiad math while behaving normally elsewhere, No Reasoning SFT is the most promising technique, U-generated Reasoning SFT consistently degrades performance due to disagreement between the model's reasoning and the trusted model's outputs, and RL through CoT is unreliable except under unrealistically favorable conditions; moreover, the elicitation observed is largely explained by the techniques broadly degrading system-prompt-following rather than removing any real aversion to sandbagging.

effect.metric: elicitation of sandbagged performance by Blue Team SFT techniques
effect.value: Blue Team techniques consistently elicit substantial portions of sandbagger performance, but by degrading system-prompt-following broadly rather than removing an aversion to sandbagging specifically

contradicts_or_qualifies: Qualifies prior work showing plain on-distribution SFT is effective (Supervised fine-tuning as a method for training-based AI control) by showing that off-distribution Blue Team elicitation techniques work for an unintended reason (degrading system-prompt-following broadly), not by removing an aversion to sandbagging
stated_future_work: Try these methods on trained model organisms where sandbagging doesn't come from the system prompt, once robust trained MOs can be built
Whether training generalizes across the no-reasoning/reasoning distribution shift against a model motivated to exploit it is left as an open question
Determine to what extent filtering disagreeing U-reasoning/T-output samples is needed to avoid performance degradation on tasks without a clear answer
limitations_stated: Results should not be interpreted as confirmation that No Reasoning SFT is an effective training technique; success was due to removing system-prompt-following, which would not generalize to models that sandbag from their own volition
Had trouble making trained model organisms robust to weak Blue Team techniques like Pirate Training, so that setting was not explored
For tasks without a clear objective answer, U's reasoning and T's outputs may never perfectly line up, making the U-generated Reasoning SFT filtering approach hard to apply
quote: Our work should thus be interpreted as: we found problems that we think make U-generated Reasoning SFT and RL through CoT unviable techniques, and we didn't find any such problems for No Reasoning SFT.
